news.title: Earnings Update: UltraTech Cement Limited (NSE:ULTRACEMCO) Just Reported Its Full-Year Results And Analysts Are Updating Their Forecasts
news.body: Shareholders might have noticed that UltraTech Cement Limited ( NSE:ULTRACEMCO ) filed its annual result this time last...

news.title: Full year 2026 earnings: Revenues and EPS in line with analyst expectations
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹278 (up from ₹205 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹890.9b (up 17% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹81.7b (up 35% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 9.2% (up from 8.0% in FY 2025). The increase in margin was driven by higher revenue. Revenue was in line with analyst estimates. Earnings per share (EPS) were also in line with analyst expectations. Revenue is forecast to grow 10% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 1.0% decline forecast for the Basic Materials industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 11% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 17% per year, which means it is tracking significantly ahead of earnings growth.

news.title: ULTRACEMCO: Capacity Expansion Will Drive Future Upside Despite GST Disputes
news.body: Analysts have revised their 12 month fair value estimate for UltraTech Cement to ₹13,636 from ₹14,045, reflecting updated assumptions for revenue growth, profit margins and forward P/E multiples. What's in the News Commissioning of 8.7 mtpa of new cement grinding capacity across Shahjahanpur in Uttar Pradesh, Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and Patratu in Jharkhand, taking domestic grey cement capacity to 200.1 mtpa and global capacity to 205.5 mtpa (company disclosure).

news.title: ULTRACEMCO: Expanding Capacity Will Drive Future Upside Despite Ongoing GST Disputes
news.body: The analyst fair value estimate for UltraTech Cement has moved slightly from ₹14,090.92 to ₹14,044.87, with the adjustment linked to modest tweaks in the discount rate, revenue growth, profit margin and future P/E assumptions as analysts refine their models. What's in the News UltraTech Cement received multiple GST orders from state and central authorities in Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Haryana related to alleged ineligible or excess Input Tax Credit and supplies to customers later deemed non existent, with combined tax demands, interest and penalties across various years that the company plans to contest, while indicating it does not expect a material financial impact.

news.title: Jindal Power, Vedanta and Havells Reportedly Among 22 Bidders for Gupta Power
news.body: Jindal Power Limited, Vedanta Limited (NSEI:VEDL) and Havells India Limited (NSEI:HAVELLS) are among 22 prospective bidders that have submitted expressions of interest (EoIs) to acquire debt-laden Gupta Power Infrastructure Limited, which has admitted debtor claims of INR 42,400 million and is undergoing insolvency proceedings, people aware of the development told ET. The company, which is a manufacturer of cables, wire rods, and conductors, is being resolved under the corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP). Other interested bidders include UltraTech Cement Limited (NSEI:ULTRACEMCO), Waaree Energies Limited (NSEI:WAAREEENER), Torrent Electricals (TCL Cables Private Limited) and Himadri Speciality Chemical Limited (BSE:500184), Orissa Metaliks Private Limited and Abci Infrastructure

news.title: ULTRACEMCO: GST Disputes And New Capacity Will Guide Balanced Outlook
news.body: Analysts have slightly increased their price target on UltraTech Cement from ₹13,965.85 to ₹14,061.95, citing updated assumptions for revenue growth, profit margins, discount rate and future P/E multiple in their valuation work. What's in the News Multiple GST enforcement orders issued to UltraTech Cement by authorities in Tamil Nadu for alleged excess Input Tax Credit (ITC) in FY 2021-22 and FY 2019-20, with combined tax demands of about ₹10.36m and ₹93.54m, along with associated interest and penalties.

news.title: ULTRACEMCO: Expanded Capacity And Contested GST Demands Will Shape Bullish Outlook
news.body: Analysts have adjusted their price target for UltraTech Cement from ₹13,784.90 to ₹13,965.85, reflecting updated assumptions around the discount rate, revenue growth, profit margin and future P/E expectations. What's in the News UltraTech Cement commissioned additional cement capacity of 1.8 mtpa across Dhule in Maharashtra and Nathdwara in Rajasthan, taking total domestic grey cement capacity to 188.66 mtpa and global capacity to 194.06 mtpa, including 5.4 mtpa overseas (Key Developments).

news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings: EPS and revenues exceed analyst expectations
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹58.66 (up from ₹50.99 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹218.3b (up 27% from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹17.3b (up 17% from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 7.9% (down from 8.5% in 3Q 2025). The decrease in margin was driven by higher expenses. Revenue exceeded analyst estimates by 5.1%. Earnings per share (EPS) also surpassed analyst estimates by 14%. Revenue is forecast to grow 11% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, while revenues in the Basic Materials industry in India are expected to remain flat. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 9% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 23% per year, which means it is tracking significantly ahead of earnings growth.
